# propsens

> **Would another, equally good propensity model have matched the same
> patients?**

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/mostafa-abbas/propsens/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mostafa-abbas/propsens/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![License:
MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

A matched study estimates each patient’s propensity score with one
model, usually logistic regression, and pairs every treated patient with
an untreated patient who has a similar score. Another model that fits
the data just as well, such as Bayesian additive regression trees (BART)
or a generalized random forest (GRF), can order the patients differently
and so pick different partners. propsens measures how much the matched
design depends on that choice, **without looking at outcomes**, so it
can be run at the design stage, next to the usual balance table.

![One treated (catheterized) patient on the left, linked to four equally
good propensity models (logistic regression and BART with seeds 1, 2 and
3). Each model places the patient at a slightly different percentile
rank and pairs the patient with a different untreated patient, A to
D.](articles/rhc-partners.png)

One treated (catheterized) patient on the left, linked to four equally
good propensity models (logistic regression and BART with seeds 1, 2 and
3). Each model places the patient at a slightly different percentile
rank and pairs the patient with a different untreated patient, A to D.

## propsens in one minute

![Four panels joined by arrows under the heading propsens in one minute.
You give it: patient characteristics and treatment, no outcomes. It
does: three kinds of model, a barrier for the quality gate, and matched
pairs. You get: kept models, rank disagreement, pair instability, and a
warning if fewer than two pass. You use it to: report next to balance,
check your design, compare effects across
models.](articles/img/one-minute.png)

Four panels joined by arrows under the heading propsens in one minute.
You give it: patient characteristics and treatment, no outcomes. It
does: three kinds of model, a barrier for the quality gate, and matched
pairs. You get: kept models, rank disagreement, pair instability, and a
warning if fewer than two pass. You use it to: report next to balance,
check your design, compare effects across models.

|  |  |
|----|----|
| **You give it** | Your study data (patient characteristics and treatment, no outcomes) and your matching settings, or your existing `MatchIt` object. |
| **It does** | Fits seven propensity models, keeps those as good as the best (the quality gate), and repeats your matching with each kept model. |
| **You get** | The list of kept models; rank disagreement (how much patients’ positions move between kept models); pair instability (how often kept models choose different partners); the balance of each model’s match; a clear warning if fewer than two models pass. |
| **You use it to** | \(1\) Report it next to your balance table, at the design stage, before looking at outcomes. (2) If the warning appears, revisit the matching design first. (3) If disagreement is noticeable, report the effect estimate under each kept model as a sensitivity analysis, as in the [heart catheterization example](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/articles/how-it-works.html). |

``` r

# Your study data and your matching settings:
propensity_sensitivity(treated ~ age + sex + diabetes, data = study_data,
                       replace = FALSE, caliper = 0.2)

# Or your existing MatchIt object (its matching settings are read from the object):
propensity_sensitivity(matched)
```

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mostafa-abbas/propsens")
```

To also build the vignettes:

``` r

remotes::install_github("mostafa-abbas/propsens", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

The heart catheterization example in the articles was pre-computed from
the public right heart catheterization data of the `ATbounds` package
(`install.packages("ATbounds")`); the script is
`data-raw/heart_catheterization_example.R`.

## What it does

propsens takes the analyst’s matched design (a `MatchIt` object, or a
formula and a data frame) and:

- **refits the propensity model** with logistic regression, BART and GRF
  (three seeds for each tree algorithm, cross-fitted scores), seven
  models in all;
- **re-matches** with each model, using the analyst’s own matching
  options;
- **applies a quality gate**: a model is kept only if it predicts
  treatment about as well as the best model and its matched sample is
  about as well balanced;
- **reports, for the kept models**, rank disagreement (how differently
  the models order the treated patients), pair instability (how often
  they choose different partners), the bootstrap rank instability of the
  logistic model, and the spread of balance across models.

## Example result (right heart catheterization)

On the public right heart catheterization data (Connors et al., *JAMA*
1996; 5,735 patients, 2,184 catheterized):

- **4 of 7 models were kept by the quality gate**: logistic regression
  and BART with seeds 1, 2 and 3. The three GRF fits were excluded.
- **Rank disagreement was 0.047.**
- **Odds ratios of death within 30 days**, matching with each kept model
  (95 % confidence interval): logistic regression 1.37 (1.19–1.57); BART
  seed 1 1.27 (1.11–1.47); BART seed 2 1.32 (1.15–1.53); BART seed 3
  1.38 (1.20–1.60). propsens itself never uses the outcome; the odds
  ratios only show what the disagreement means for the estimate.

The [step-by-step
article](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/articles/how-it-works.html)
walks through this example.

## Example

``` r

library(propsens)
data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
matched <- MatchIt::matchit(treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
                            data = lalonde, distance = "glm", replace = FALSE)
sensitivity <- propensity_sensitivity(matched)  # refits the seven models and re-matches
sensitivity                                     # gate, rank disagreement, pair instability
summary(sensitivity)                            # every number, every model's fit and balance
plot(sensitivity, type = "models")              # balance after matching, one row per model
```

On these data no model passes the balance part of the gate, so the
output opens with a warning that the diagnostic is outside the setting
where it was evaluated. The run takes about a minute.

## What it is, and what it is not

**What it is:** a design-stage description of how much a 1:1
nearest-neighbour matched design depends on the choice of propensity
model, at the level of the whole study.

**What it is not:** a test of whether the effect estimate is right, a
per-patient flag, or a check for unmeasured confounding. Every model
uses the same covariates, so a confounder missing from that list is
missing from all of them.

The diagnostics are evaluated in a manuscript in preparation (Abbas, Do
equally good propensity models agree on whom to match?). Until it is
available, report the output as a description of how much the matched
design depends on the choice of propensity model, not as a validated
check.

## Documentation

The articles are also on the website,
<https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens>.

- **Getting started:**
  [`vignette("getting-started", package = "propsens")`](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/articles/getting-started.md).
- **propsens at a glance:**
  [`vignette("at-a-glance", package = "propsens")`](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/articles/at-a-glance.md)
  ([source](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/vignettes/at-a-glance.Rmd)):
  the question, what you run, what you get and how to read it, with the
  right heart catheterization example.
- **How propsens works, step by step:**
  [`vignette("how-it-works", package = "propsens")`](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/articles/how-it-works.md)
  ([source](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/vignettes/how-it-works.Rmd)):
  propensity scores and matching, the three kinds of model, the quality
  gate, rank disagreement and pair instability, and effect estimates
  across the kept models, each with the same example.
- **How the diagnostics are defined:**
  [`vignette("definitions", package = "propsens")`](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/articles/definitions.md).
- **Reading the plots and reporting:**
  [`vignette("reporting", package = "propsens")`](https://mostafa-abbas.github.io/propsens/articles/reporting.md).
- **Citing:** `citation("propsens")`.
